candidates.product_observable: One fixed learner uses cross-task experience plus bounded current-task feedback to predict and rank unseen typed action-primitive compositions.

legal_packet.legal_actions: canonical typed primitive-composition descriptors without action, task or split IDs
legal_packet.history: prior legal observations, chosen composition descriptors and observed bounded outcomes
legal_packet.feedback: bounded scalar outcome for the chosen legal composition only

candidates.statistical_identifiability_assumption: Train tasks expose reusable primitive effects; held-out tasks contain novel primitive compositions, and bounded legal feedback identifies a task-local residual without exposing private task identity.
candidates.identifiability_test_plan: A candidate-independent future screen must compare current-observation-only, legal full-history, no-meta and budget-faithful feasible-reference predictions on exact-zero-overlap held-out compositions at transfer and adaptation checkpoints.
candidates.identifiability_kill_criterion: Reject if the legal feasible reference cannot separate from observation/no-feedback/lookup controls on both axes, if legal history adds no information on the adaptation axis, or if held-out composition lookup coverage is nonzero.

capability_axes.forward_transfer: At zero or few held-out feedback steps, cross-task structure improves novel-composition prediction over no-meta, descriptor-blind lookup and from-scratch controls.
capability_axes.within_task_adaptation: At later checkpoints, legal held-out outcomes improve task-local predictions over frozen-global, no-update and no-feedback controls.

mechanism_challengers_and_capability_riv: per-task specialist panel as breadth rival

budget_faithful_feasible_reference.model: regularized compositional GLM with online task-local residual update
budget_faithful_feasible_reference.admission_role: Required to show that both axes are reachable from the legal channel under the frozen budget; it supplies no candidate or mechanism claim.

diagnostic_ideal_ceiling.model: exact visible-channel hierarchical Bayes or mixed-effects posterior

decode_and_saturation_risks.observation_decode: Typed descriptors may directly determine outcomes if the generator lacks hidden task-local variation.
decode_and_saturation_risks.history_decode: A static full-history decoder may saturate if adaptation requires no mutable state beyond the packet.
decode_and_saturation_risks.lookup_cache: Novel-composition coverage is fake if held-out tuples or equivalent canonical keys occur in train.
decode_and_saturation_risks.specialist: A per-task specialist may dominate narrow tasks but is a rival, not an invalidating control.

required_ablations: permute action descriptors while preserving semantics
bypass predictor with declared neutral scorer
candidates.replay_design: Fresh-process recomputation from serialized model/update state plus current legal observation and action descriptors; stored predictions and actions are forbidden.
candidates.smallest_falsifier: Exact held-out composition lookup coverage is nonzero, or no-meta/no-update controls erase either headroom axis under equal access.
candidates.expected_negative_mode: Static descriptor decoding or tuple memorization explains the apparent transfer, while legal feedback adds no independent task-local information.
material_difference_from_closed_surface: typed compositional actions instead of a fixed eight-action set
cross-task shared structure plus task-local residual instead of one static hidden 8-bit latent
held-out composition split instead of latent-parity split
separate forward-transfer and adaptation axes instead of one posterior-inference aggregate
fresh generator, schema, seeds, controls and artifact namespace

epistemic_status.fact: The closed surface used fixed actions, a static hidden latent and a different split/metric family.
epistemic_status.inference: Compositional novelty plus task-local residuals may separate transfer from adaptation with simpler instrumentation.
epistemic_status.assumption: A legal feasible reference can achieve nontrivial performance on both axes.
epistemic_status.unknown: Actual oracle-to-control headroom and minimum detectable effects have not been computed.

candidates.product_observable: One fixed learner predicts outcomes of legal interventions on held-out attributed graph motifs and adapts to task-local affordance changes from observed outcomes.

legal_packet.current_observation: visible attributed local graph and query context
legal_packet.history: prior visible graphs, chosen legal interventions and observed bounded outcomes
legal_packet.feedback: bounded intervention outcome on the chosen graph/action pair

candidates.statistical_identifiability_assumption: Visible attributed motifs and legal intervention history contain enough information to infer reusable causal-affordance structure without private graph access.
candidates.identifiability_test_plan: A candidate-independent future screen must compare observation-only, fitted legal full-history, graph lookup and budget-faithful graph-reference predictions on graph-isomorphism-deduplicated held-out motifs before and after legal local feedback.
candidates.identifiability_kill_criterion: Reject if held-out motifs canonicalize to train signatures, if observation-only/graph-lookup/no-feedback/no-update controls saturate either required axis, or if the budget-faithful feasible reference cannot separate from those invalidating controls.

capability_axes.forward_transfer: Cross-graph structure improves prediction on held-out motifs before substantial local feedback.
capability_axes.within_task_adaptation: Observed intervention outcomes update a local affordance belief and improve later predictions.

mechanism_challengers_and_capability_riv: fitted static legal full-history graph decoder

budget_faithful_feasible_reference.model: bounded graph-feature/message-passing regressor with online local-affordance residual update
budget_faithful_feasible_reference.admission_role: Required legal-channel reachability reference for both axes; it cannot establish candidate or causal-mechanism validity.

decode_and_saturation_risks.observation_decode: Graph attributes may encode the target directly.
decode_and_saturation_risks.history_decode: A static graph-history model may make mutable adaptation unnecessary.
decode_and_saturation_risks.lookup_cache: Graph canonicalization may collapse held-out motifs onto seen signatures.
decode_and_saturation_risks.specialist: Motif specialists may hide lack of breadth.

required_ablations: permute node identifiers while preserving graph isomorphism
candidates.replay_design: Fresh-process recomputation from serialized learned graph state plus the visible graph and legal interventions, with isomorphism-preserving counterfactuals.
candidates.mechanism_attribution_downgrade: If a fitted static legal full-history graph decoder matches, block any claim that an explicit mutable online-update mechanism is required, but do not by that fact alone reject bounded product capability.
candidates.smallest_falsifier: Graph lookup, observation-only or no-feedback/no-update controls saturate a required axis, the feasible reference is unreachable under parity, or held-out motifs are canonical aliases of train motifs.
candidates.expected_negative_mode: Graph representation leakage or canonical lookup explains the result, and the instrument becomes more complex than the capability separator.
material_difference_from_closed_surface: variable attributed graphs and interventions instead of fixed vector contexts/actions
held-out graph motifs rather than latent-state parity
fresh graph generator, schema, seeds, baselines and artifacts

epistemic_status.fact: No graph surface, generator or graph-specific artifact currently exists in this route.
epistemic_status.inference: Graph motif transfer could test a stronger form of structural outcome learning.
epistemic_status.assumption: Legal attributed graphs support a non-private feasible reference.
epistemic_status.unknown: Whether graph leakage and instrument complexity leave fair measurable headroom.

candidates.product_observable: One fixed learner attributes delayed bounded outcomes to action sequences and adapts after hidden regime changes.

legal_packet.history: prior legal observations/actions plus delayed outcome events when they arrive

candidates.statistical_identifiability_assumption: Aggregate delayed outcomes contain enough legal information to identify both reusable sequence structure and a changed local regime within the bounded horizon.
candidates.identifiability_test_plan: A future redesign would need a candidate-independent observational-equivalence test over legal event histories and a budget-faithful sequence reference before this surface could be reconsidered under a new selection task.
candidates.identifiability_kill_criterion: Current paper screen rejects because multiple private per-step credit assignments may remain legal-channel equivalent and no budget-faithful legal reference has yet been shown to separate those equivalents.

capability_axes.forward_transfer: Cross-task sequence structure improves early held-out outcome prediction.
capability_axes.within_task_adaptation: Delayed feedback after a regime change updates future sequence rankings.

budget_faithful_feasible_reference.model: bounded fitted hidden-state sequence model with online legal-event filtering
budget_faithful_feasible_reference.admission_role: NOT_YET_SHOWN_FEASIBLE; absence of a demonstrated legal-channel reference supports the current paper rejection.

diagnostic_ideal_ceiling.model: exact legal-event Bayesian change-point and sequence posterior

decode_and_saturation_risks.observation_decode: Visible regime-correlated context may reveal the switch.
decode_and_saturation_risks.history_decode: A static change-point decoder may reproduce all adaptation behavior.
decode_and_saturation_risks.lookup_cache: Repeated sequence bundles may make episodic traversal sufficient.
decode_and_saturation_risks.specialist: Per-regime specialists may not expose a shared learner.

candidates.replay_design: Fresh-process recomputation from serialized sequence/update state and the legal event stream, including counterfactual feedback timing.
candidates.mechanism_attribution_downgrade: If a legal recency/change-point or fitted full-history model matches, block special online-credit/update attribution; product capability would require separate bounded evaluation rather than automatic rejection.
candidates.smallest_falsifier: Multiple private credit assignments remain observationally equivalent on the legal channel or no budget-faithful legal feasible reference exists under the bounded horizon.
candidates.expected_negative_mode: Delayed aggregate feedback is underidentified, so apparent learning depends on private credit labels or a simple regime heuristic.
material_difference_from_closed_surface: delayed sequential credit and regime change rather than one-step Bernoulli feedback
sequence-family novelty instead of fixed action probes
fresh event schema, generator, seeds, controls and artifacts

epistemic_status.fact: The proposed legal channel withholds private per-step causal credit.
epistemic_status.inference: That withholding creates a serious identifiability risk at a bounded horizon.
epistemic_status.assumption: A redesigned legal event channel might later resolve the ambiguity, but that is not established here.
epistemic_status.unknown: Whether any fair non-private reference can separate reusable learning from recency/change-point controls.

no_go_option.meaning: Select no successor and keep the learned-outcome route closed without preregistration or implementation.

basis: cleanest material break from the fixed-action/static-latent closed surface
two separately falsifiable transfer and adaptation axes
lower instrument complexity and leakage surface than the graph alternative
fewer identifiability risks than delayed aggregate credit assignment

claim_ceiling: Operator decision support and qualitative paper collision screening only; no empirical headroom, surface admission, preregistration, learning, mechanism, product, runtime, mainline, agency, subjectivity or consciousness claim.
